commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Size the KV cache from the groups HiSparse allocates
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

With HiSparse, a GPU pool too small for one `max_model_len` request passes the startup check, and requests then wait forever with no error ([report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55398#issuecomment-5903470382): `--num-gpu-blocks-override 160`, two 6k prompts never run).

The startup check sized HiSparse from the model's grouped specs rather than the groups HiSparse actually allocates. So it counted only indexer pages, missing the resident and hot groups, and used the wrong block size for the override.

## Changes

- HiSparse's grouping hook now returns the groups it allocates, and workers report its derived resident/hot caches. The standard startup check, override conversion and cross-rank sync then work for HiSparse unchanged.
- KV cache layout resolution skips specs without per-layer views, such as these caches, which lay out their own raw backing.
- Resident groups are sized by their admission window (`max_admission_blocks_per_request`), which #59494 now enforces at runtime.
- Auto-fit uses the startup check's criterion, so it can't pick a length that check rejects.
- Removed the HiSparse-specific memory estimate and the cross-worker `min(available_memory)` workaround.
- Projection returns a group unchanged when all its layers are on the worker, so HiSparse's group flags survive.

A pool that can't hold one request now fails the standard "max seq len" check at startup, before KV cache allocation.

## Test Plan

- Unit test: a 160-block pool is rejected at `max_model_len=8192`, and the boundary is exact at 32768 with 2048 tokens in flight (656 blocks rejected, 657 accepted). Auto-fit with 657 blocks starts. Layout resolution is unaffected by the derived caches.
- B200 (shrunk GLM-5.3, dummy weights), on this branch merged with #59494: TP=1 and TP=2 including ranks with unequal memory, 131k context, auto-fit, the reported setup, and `test_hisparse.py`.

## Test Result

- Unit tests pass.
- B200, this branch (includes #59494):
  - Too-small pools fail at startup: 160 blocks at 8192, 2400 blocks at 131072.
  - Pools that fit serve: 1000 blocks at 8192, auto-fit, and 3200 or 4000 blocks at 131072 with a 120k-token prompt. Without #59494, the 4000-block case livelocks.
  - TP=2 serves, including with unequal ranks.
  - The reported setup at 700 blocks: both 6k prompts complete.
  - `test_hisparse.py`: 4 passed.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][PCP] Shard decode requests across PCP ranks
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose PCP currently replicates every decode request on every PCP rank. For PCP-only deployments (`DCP == 1`), every rank already has a complete KV-cache replica, so this repeats the same decode computation `pcp_size` times. This PR: - assigns decode-only rows round-robin across PCP ranks on every scheduler step; - keeps the existing DualChunkSwap prefill partitioning unchanged; - gathers the owner-produced MLA and sparse-indexer KV updates so every PCP rank retains a complete cache replica; - preserves replicated decode when `DCP > 1`, because each DCP rank must consume its local KV shard. **Design trade-off.** This approach distributes decode requests across the PCP group in a data-parallel fashion and removes redundant decode computation. However, keeping the replicated KV cache consistent across PCP ranks requires additional communication to propagate the owner-produced KV updates. This compute-communication trade-off makes the realized gains smaller and more workload-dependent than the ideal reduction in redundant computation would suggest. ### Duplicate-work check I searched open PCP/decode issues and PRs before submission. This does not duplicate: - #49564, which adds FlashAttention/GQA PCP and PCP+DCP prefill support but does not shard PCP-only decode requests; - #49517, which replaces replicated KV-update collectives with opt-in, model-specific direct peer stores but does not reduce replicated decode computation; - #49741, which owner-shards persistent KV history for capacity rather than sharding decode compute. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Keep batch-invariance NCCL pins out of the weight-transfer group
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` pins `NCCL_ALGO`, `NCCL_PROTO`, the channel count and a few related variables in the worker's environment. NCCL never reconciles these across ranks. An external trainer that does not carry them therefore deadlocks with the workers in the warm-up `all_reduce` of the weight-transfer group, or a worker fails with `ncclInternalError`.

The pins only matter for vLLM's own collectives, so this PR keeps them out of the communicators shared with the trainer:

- `vllm.utils.nccl.pin_nccl_env(pins)` sets the pins and records the values they replace. It also lists the pins in `NCCL_NO_CACHE`, so NCCL re-reads them for each communicator instead of caching the first value. `override_envs_for_invariance` now pins its NCCL settings through it.
- `vllm.utils.nccl.unpinned_nccl_env()` restores the launch values while `stateless_init_process_group` / `uid_init_process_group` create the trainer-facing communicator, then puts the pins back. Every NCCL weight-transfer engine creates its group through these two functions.
- `NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE` stays a plain process-wide setting, because NCCL keeps it in a global.
- On ROCm, or when the NCCL library vLLM loads is older than 2.29.7 or cannot be loaded, there is no `NCCL_NO_CACHE`, so nothing is lifted. In that case vLLM logs a warning, once, when a shared communicator is built.

The trainer needs no change. The transfer group uses the environment both sides were launched with, as for any NCCL group. Copying vLLM's pins into the trainer is no longer needed and would now cause a mismatch. If `NCCL_ALGO`, `NCCL_PROTO` or the channel limits are set only in an `nccl.conf` file rather than exported, the worker cannot see them when it restores the launch values, so export them instead.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py`. `test_nccl_weight_transfer_between_processes` gains a `batch-invariant-worker` case: the worker applies the pins and builds a pinned NCCL communicator first, as vLLM's own groups do; the trainer stays unpinned.
- End-to-end on 4x GB300, `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (NCCL 2.29.7), Qwen3-0.6B:
  - The server runs `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` with TP2, and separately with PP2.
  - An unmodified external trainer, with no batch-invariance env, runs 3 rounds of `pause → NCCL weight update → resume`. Each round sends 1.5 GB.
  - Before and after every round, one prompt is sent alone and inside a batch of 16, and the tokens and logprobs are compared.

## Test Result

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `batch-invariant-worker` test | times out (deadlock) | passes |
| same test with the `NCCL_NO_CACHE` line removed from this PR | — | fails, so the test depends on the mechanism |
| `test_weight_transfer.py` on 2 GPUs | — | all passed |
| e2e TP2 / PP2 | all ranks hang in the warm-up `ncclAllReduce` | 3/3 rounds each; batch invariance holds and outputs are identical before and after |

NCCL INFO logs on the worker show vLLM's TP communicators at 1 channel before and after the transfer group is built. The transfer group uses NCCL defaults on all ranks.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Seed derender detokenization from the prompt
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On SentencePiece tokenizers (Llama-2, Phi-3), `/v1/chat/completions/derender` and `/v1/completions/derender` drop the first output token's leading space but the main endpoints keep it. The engine seeds its detokenizer with the prompt while derender decoded the output tokens with no prompt context.

Derender now seeds its decode window from the prompt tail too. That covers batch chat and completions, streaming with and without a parser, and streaming completions. Each derender request takes an optional `prompt_token_ids` (the `token_ids` from `/render`). If it's missing, derender uses the generate response's `prompt_token_ids`. If that's missing too, it decodes as before and logs a warning once. Nothing breaks for existing callers.

Other changes:
- The batch paths now go through the same incremental `_detokenize_delta` as streaming, so `clean_up_tokenization_spaces` no longer applies there. That matches what the engine does.
- `_detokenize_delta` trims its window after every token, so long batch decodes stay linear.
- `prompt_token_ids` is capped at `max_model_len`, like the other caller- upplied token lists.
- Derender now works out `skip_special_tokens` and `spaces_between_special_tokens` the same way the engine does. Before, the parser paths hardcoded `skip_special_tokens=False` and never passed `spaces_between_special_tokens`, so a request with `spaces_between_special_tokens: false` could decode differently. The fast/slow detokenizer check is now a shared helper (`uses_fast_detokenizer()`) used by both the engine and derender, so the slow path matches too.

Fixes #59043. Reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/42729#issuecomment-5857086699.

Also fixes #59089. When the output stopped mid-character (e.g. `max_tokens` cutting an emoji), batch derender decoded the whole id list in one go and tacked a `�` on the end. The engine holds those partial bytes back and so does streaming derender. As the batch paths now go through `_detokenize_delta` (same as streaming), they get the same hold-back, so the trailing `�` is gone. Added a unit test that cuts 🌈 one byte short and checks batch, streaming and the engine's `DecodeStream` all give the same text.

## Test Plan

`pytest -s -v tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py`
`pytest -s -v tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py`

The new unit tests use the tiny Llama (Metaspace) tokenizer and compare each decode path against a `DecodeStream` primed with the prompt. The HTTP tests check that seeded output gains exactly the leading space and that the new length and bounds checks return 400.

## Test Result

All tests pass.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Parse tool calls and reasoning from checkpoint response templates
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Use checkpoint `response_template` metadata to parse reasoning, content, and tool calls with one unified `Parser`, so a checkpoint that ships this metadata can be served without a model-specific parser.

### Activation

- The parser is registered as `hf`, a regular tool and reasoning parser: `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hf` parses tools from the template's `tool_calls` field, and `--reasoning-parser hf` parses reasoning from its `thinking` field. The name mirrors `--tokenizer-mode hf`: both run the checkpoint's own Hugging Face metadata instead of model-specific code, and the Rust frontend's parser uses the same name. Either can be used alone; `ParserManager` combines them into one parser, like the other unified parsers.
- It cannot be combined with another tool or reasoning parser, and Harmony models keep `HarmonyParser`.
- Metadata is read from the runtime tokenizer. Startup fails if it is missing or invalid, lacks the field a selected parser needs, or has defaults serving cannot route. Servers without a tokenizer (`skip_tokenizer_init`) still start.
- A server or request chat template is allowed but logs a warning, since the parser still expects the checkpoint's output format.

### Parsing

- `ResponseTemplateParser` implements `Parser` directly and turns `chat_parsing` region events into deltas. The template parser is text-only, so it does not go through `ParserEngine`, which is unchanged.
- `ResponseTemplateReasoningParser` is a plain `ReasoningParser`: it tells the parser and the structured-output engine where reasoning ends, and supplies the thinking markers for the thinking budget.
- A tool call is emitted whole, name and arguments together, once its region closes and parses. A region still open at the end of the stream, for example because its closer is also a stop token, is parsed from the generated text; a call that does not parse is dropped with a warning. A name is not streamed from the opener alone because the opener can match only part of the name: Gemma 4's `call:(?P<name>\w+)` matches `get` in `get-weather`.
- Unknown tool names are forwarded.
- `Parser.set_prompt_token_ids` hands parsers the rendered prompt, so regions opened by the prompt continue correctly.
- The structured-output reasoning gate ends as soon as the prompt ends in a content or tool-call opener, so the first content token is constrained even when that opener is still held back as a possible longer delimiter.
- During decoding, the gate checks whether the new tokens end in a literal thinking closer instead of decoding and reparsing the whole output at every step.
- String arguments are coerced by the tool schema in `chat_parsing`, like Transformers.

### Serving

- Chat Completions, Responses, and the derender path pass the rendered prompt to the parser, including for non-streaming and batched output.
- Strict tools, required and named tool choice, and `parallel_tool_calls=False` are rejected until a format-compatible structural grammar can enforce them.

### Shared parser changes

These touch `abstract_parser.py`, which every parser uses, and default to current behavior:

- `Parser.set_prompt_token_ids` (no-op by default) gives non-streaming parsing the prompt that `parse_delta` already receives.
- The `always_adjust_request` class flag (off by default) makes the renderer call `adjust_request` even with `tool_choice="none"` and no reasoning parser, since template delimiters can be special tokens around plain content.

**Stack**

1. #58602: port the `chat_parsing` core.
2. #58603: enrich the streaming events serving needs.
3. This PR: parse checkpoint response templates in Chat Completions and Responses.

#58602 and #58603 are merged, so every commit here belongs to this PR.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR adds `response_template` parsing to serving (searched open PRs for `response_template`, `response template`, `chat_parsing`, and `chat parsing`).

**AI assistance.** This PR was written with AI assistance (Cursor, and Claude Code for the last three commits). Every changed line was reviewed and the tests below were run.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/parser/test_chat_parsing.py tests/parser/test_response_template.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_streaming_events.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_parsable_context_unit.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py -v
pytest tests/parser tests/tool_parsers tests/reasoning
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only main...HEAD)
```

## Test Result

- Response-template, `chat_parsing`, Responses streaming-event, parsable-context, and derender-stream unit tests pass (216 passed, 1 xfailed). New tests cover parser selection and startup validation and a decode-time reasoning gate that never decodes.
- `tests/parser`, `tests/tool_parsers`, and `tests/reasoning` show no regressions: the set of failing tests on my machine (fixtures that need a GPU device) is identical with and without this PR.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, and `typos` are clean on the changed files.
- After the rename to `hf`, the `chat_parsing`, response-template, Responses streaming-event, and parsable-context tests pass (172 passed), including a new regression test that the chat serving objects start without a tokenizer.
- After implementing `Parser` directly and emitting calls when their region parses: `tests/parser` (except `tests/parser/cohere`, which needs the optional `cohere_melody` package), `tests/reasoning`, the Responses streaming-event, parsable-context, and derender-stream tests (server fixtures included), the batched prompt-prefix test, and the tokenizer-less startup test give 6333 passed. The 25 failures (Mistral grammar factory tests and one Lark structural-tag test) are identical on the base commit and come from local `xgrammar` / `mistral_common` versions. `pre-commit`, including mypy 3.10 and 3.12, is clean.
- The GPU-backed tests (`test_serving_chat.py`, `test_cli_args.py`, `test_batched_chat_completions.py`, and the server fixtures in `test_derender_stream.py`) rely on CI.

No model evaluation yet. Output only changes when a deployment selects the `hf` parser; existing parsers and default serving are unaffected. I can add end-to-end results with a checkpoint that ships `response_template` metadata.

commits.pr_title: [Distributed] Enable custom all-reduce under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
commits.pr_body:
Fixes #50136 ## Problem `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` forces custom all-reduce off and runs every TP all-reduce through NCCL pinned to one channel. Custom all-reduce cannot simply be re-enabled because `should_custom_ar()` picks the backend by tensor size, and the tensor is `[num_tokens, hidden]`: ```mermaid flowchart LR A["all-reduce [tokens, hidden]"] --> B{"bytes < 8 MiB?"} B -- "yes (decode, small prefill)" --> C["custom kernel
fp32 accumulate, round once"] B -- "no (large prefill batch)" --> D["NCCL
rounds to bf16 at every tree step"] ``` The same request is reduced by different summation orders depending on what else the scheduler batched with it. Measured on 4xH100, TP=4, bf16: NCCL and the custom kernel disagree in 33% of output elements. End to end (Qwen2.5-1.5B, bs=1 vs bs=24, custom all-reduce on): 24/24 prompts diverge, starting at position 0. ## Fix Under batch invariance, make the backend choice size-independent and keep the custom kernel on a fixed reduction order: 1. Stop forcing `disable_custom_all_reduce` (`config/parallel.py`). 2. `should_custom_ar()` ignores the size threshold; `all_reduce()` reduces inputs above `max_size` in `max_size` chunks. The 1-stage kernel sums each element independently in rank order 0..N-1, so chunking is bit-exact (`custom_all_reduce.py`). 3. Pin `VLLM_CUSTOM_ALLREDUCE_ALGO=1stage` in `override_envs_for_invariance()`. The 2-stage kernel rotates the rank order per slice, which is size-dependent (fp32: 20-30% of elements differ between sizes). 4. Gate AITER all-reduce and QuickReduce off under batch invariance, next to the existing FlashInfer gate. Without the forced disable they would become reachable on ROCm, and neither has a fixed reduction order (`cuda_communicator.py`). Chunking is chosen over sizing the IPC buffer to `max_num_batched_tokens x hidden` at init: no extra memory, no model info needed in the communicator, and it works for any all-reduce shape (vision towers, MoE). Outside batch invariance nothing changes. Latency inside a CUDA graph, bf16, TP=4 H100, per all-reduce: | Size | custom 1-stage | NCCL (pinned, current BI path) | |---|---|---| | 24 KiB (decode) | 5 us | 39 us | | 8 MiB | 81 us | 693 us | ## Test plan All on H100, TP=4 unless noted. - New `test_custom_allreduce_chunked[2,4]`: 3-chunk 17.6 MiB input matches the fp32 sequential reference bitwise, eager and inside a CUDA graph. New unit test for the size gate under batch invariance. Full `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py`: 19 passed, 1 skipped (SM100-only). - `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` with `VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=4`: 22/22 pass (all attention backends), custom all-reduce now active. - `tests/v1/determinism/test_online_batch_invariance.py` with `VLLM_TP_SIZE=4`: 3/3 pass. - VLM (`Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct`, image inputs) bs=1 vs bsN at TP=4 with batch invariance: bitwise identical. - Standalone bs=1 vs bs=24 on Qwen2.5-1.5B with prefix caching off: 24/24 diverge before, 0/24 after.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Use upstream GLM-5.3 and Qwen4-Exp configs and processor
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Transformers ships `glm5_next` as of **v5.16.1** and `qwen4_exp` as of **v5.16.0**, so the vendored copies can go. Raises the `transformers` floor in `requirements/common.txt` from `>= 5.10.4` to `>= 5.16.1` — CI already pins `transformers==5.16.1` exactly in `requirements/test/{cuda,rocm,xpu}.in`, so this only makes the declared minimum match what is already tested.

Removed:

- `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/glm5_next.py` (420 lines)
- `vllm/transformers_utils/processors/glm5next.py` (953 lines)
- `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/qwen4_exp.py`
- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/config.py`

Net **-1961 lines**.

### Not a straight deletion

The upstream classes are not drop-in replacements, so the model code moves to their spellings:

| vLLM read | upstream ships |
|---|---|
| `mla_nope` | `mla_use_nope` |
| `num_experts_per_token` | `num_experts_per_tok` |
| `moe_renormalize` | `norm_topk_prob` |
| `mhc_num_residual_streams` | `hc_mult` |
| `mhc_sinkhorn_iterations` | `hc_sinkhorn_iters` |

`is_moe` / `is_kda_layer` / `is_linear_attn` now derive from `layer_types`, and text-level reads go through `hf_text_config` now that the top-level config no longer mirrors its `text_config` via `__getattribute__`.

I verified the rename table by loading the real `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` `config.json` through upstream's `Glm5NextConfig` and diffing the resolved attribute surface against every attribute the model tree reads.

### Behaviour deliberately preserved

Three things in the vendored code were intentional divergences, not schema, and are kept with their explanations:

1. **Vision `rms_norm_eps` stays 1e-6.** The checkpoint ships 1e-5 and upstream honours it; the vendored config force-overrode it because 1e-5 "produces repetitive/degraded image descriptions". Now a named constant at its single call site.
2. **The frame sampler moves to `Glm5NextVideoBackend._sample_frame_indices`**, its only consumer, rather than being replaced by upstream's `sample_frames`. See the open question below — this one is worth a second look.
3. **The `NotImplementedError` guards** for config options this implementation lacks move into `_validate_supported_config`, called from `Glm5NextModel.__init__`.

Three GLM-5.3 values have no source in either the checkpoint or the upstream config, so they become named constants rather than silently-missing attributes: `mhc_tau` (0.05), `mhc_post_mult_value` (2.0), `logit_scale` (1.0).

### Hybrid layer accounting

Both vendored configs supplied a `layers_block_type` property that mapped their sparse-attention layer type onto `"attention"`. Without it, `ModelConfig.get_num_layers_by_block_type` falls through to its `layer_types` branch, which only recognised `"full_attention"` — so both models would have counted **zero** attention layers. It now counts `deepseek_sparse_attention` and `qwen_sparse_attention` too, which is what both properties did.

`_get_full_attention_layer_indices` in the turboquant config has the same blind spot, but it already checks `layer_types` first and so is unchanged by this PR. Flagging it as a separate pre-existing issue rather than widening scope here.

### Open question: the frame sampler

This PR keeps vLLM's own frame sampler, but I am not confident that is the right call and would like a view on it.

The sampler's docstring justifies diverging from the reference implementation by noting that the linspace variant "cost 4 points on video grounding evals". That comment describes only the **short-clip** branch (`total_frames < extract_t`), which requires `fps < 2`; I could not construct a case where that branch differs from upstream at all.

The branch that does differ is the common one, for an unrelated reason: vLLM walks at `1/(temporal_patch_size * target_fps)` (0.25s), collecting ~2x the candidates, then re-spreads them with `linspace`. Upstream walks at `1/target_fps` (0.5s) and keeps its picks. Over a sweep of realistic sources, **38/53 cases differ** — same frame counts, different indices:

| case | vLLM | upstream |
|---|---|---|
| 30s @30fps | `0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 76, 91, 106` | `0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90, 105` |
| 3 frames @2fps | `0, 1, 2, 2` | `0, 1` |

vLLM's spacing drifts off the target fps and short sources pick up a duplicated tail frame from the odd-parity pad. There is also no consistency argument for keeping our own: `create_hf_metadata` sets `do_sample_frames = len(valid_frame_indices) == source.total_frames_num`, so whenever the backend sub-samples the processor is told not to re-sample, and the backend's choice is authoritative either way.

So switching to upstream's `sample_frames` would delete the last vendored piece and looks more correct on the merits — but it changes frame selection for nearly every video, so it needs a video eval that I could not run. Keeping ours (what this PR does) preserves exactly what ships today at no eval cost. Happy to switch if a reviewer with a GPU wants to take the eval.

### Dropped code left over from Qwen3-Next — please sanity-check

`Qwen4ExpDecoderLayer` selected between a MoE block and a dense `Qwen3NextMLP`:

```python
mlp_only_layers = getattr(config, "mlp_only_layers", [])
num_experts = getattr(config, "num_experts", 0) or 0
absolute_layer_id = self.layer_idx + 1
is_moe_layer = self.layer_idx not in mlp_only_layers and (
    num_experts > 0 and absolute_layer_id % config.decoder_sparse_step == 0
)
```

This is a verbatim lift of `qwen3_next.py:479-485`, which arrived with the original support PR (#53896) — Qwen4Exp derives from Qwen3-Next and still subclasses `Qwen3NextAttention` and `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock`. `decoder_sparse_step` and `mlp_only_layers` are Qwen3-Next concepts; upstream's `Qwen4ExpTextConfig` declares neither, and neither appears anywhere in `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` or `...-FP8`. They only resolved because the vendored config subclassed `Qwen3NextConfig` and inherited them, which is why nothing ever flagged the branch as dead.

Evaluating the original expression against both checkpoints with the old vendored config gives `is_moe_layer` **True for 48/48 layers**, no dense layers: with `mlp_only_layers=[]`, `num_experts=512` and `decoder_sparse_step=1` it reduces to `True` for any layer index. So this PR builds the MoE block unconditionally and drops the branch, its guards and the `Qwen3NextMLP` import (`-38/+6`).

commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #59055.

Includes the allocator change that was briefly split out as #59577 (now closed): the first two commits keep every cuMem memory pool alive when a tag is re-entered; the last two are the workspace change.

Rebased on main after #59200 (shared GPU/XPU worker init). The `xpu_worker.py` hunk is gone because XPU now shares the init path.

`WorkspaceManager` allocates its scratch buffer with a plain `torch.empty`, outside the sleep-mode memory pool, so `/sleep` never releases it.
- At TP4 it is about 1.3 GiB per GPU.
- With DP and DeepGEMM/Marlin MoE (the default allgather/reduce-scatter all2all), it grows with `dp_size × max_num_batched_tokens`. DP8 reaches 4.5 GiB per GPU.

The scratch holds nothing between forward passes. This PR allocates it in the sleep-mode pool under a new `workspace` tag:
- `/sleep` discards it; nothing is copied.
- `/wake_up` remaps it at the same virtual address, so captured CUDA graphs stay valid.
- Persistent workspace resources are unchanged.

Changes:
- `WorkspaceManager` takes an optional `alloc_context` factory, defaulting to `nullcontext`.
  - The shared `Worker._init_workspace_and_model_runner()` (#59200) passes `_maybe_get_memory_pool_context("workspace")` once, which is also a no-op when the sleep-mode allocator is off. XPU uses the same init path, so it gets the tag without an `xpu_worker.py` change.
  - CPU does not support sleep mode and is unchanged.
- Selective wake may defer only the user-facing `weights` and `kv_cache` tags (`DEFERRABLE_TAGS` in `vllm/device_allocator/__init__.py`); the CUDA and XPU allocators restore every other tag, `workspace` included, on any wake. Without it, the common RL sequence (`wake_up(["weights"])`, update weights, `wake_up(["kv_cache"])`) would leave the scratch unmapped while captured graphs still point at it. Behaviour change: allocations under tags other than `weights`/`kv_cache`, including the default tag, are now restored by any wake.
- A workspace resize enters `workspace` again while blocks of the earlier buffer can still be live, so the allocator must handle a re-entered tag. On main, every `use_memory_pool(tag)` entry creates a new `MemPool`, and entering a tag again overwrites `allocator_and_pools[tag]`, the only reference to the previous pool. Main never re-enters a tag (`weights` once, `kv_cache` once), so nothing triggers this today; this PR (`workspace`) and #59158 (`runtime`) do.
  - A tensor still alive in a dropped pool is later freed with `cudaFree` instead of `my_free` (pytorch/pytorch#146431). The new `test_reentered_tag` reproduces this on main.
  - `allocator_and_pools` now holds a list of `(pool, allocator)` entries per tag, on CUDA and XPU, and `release_pools` flattens it. Every pool stays alive until `release_pools`.
  - Each entry still gets a new pool, as on main: the exit sweep unmaps free segments behind the caching allocator, so reusing a pool could hand out an unmapped block.
  - When a tag is entered again, the free segments of its older pools are unmapped first, so an outgrown buffer is returned before the next allocation. This is the exit sweep, factored out as `_trim`. PyTorch has no per-pool `empty_cache` for a live pool (pytorch/pytorch#145168, closed, unchanged by design).
  - XPU gets only the list (it has no exit sweep), so there an outgrown buffer stays mapped until shutdown.
  - Two older open PRs read `allocator_and_pools["weights"][0]` (#23875, #49151) and would need `[-1][0]` after this change.

## Test Plan

- New unit test `test_selective_wake_restores_internal_tags[workspace|default]`: `wake_up(["weights"])` restores a `workspace` or default-tag allocation while `kv_cache` stays asleep; `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` then restores it.
- New unit test `test_workspace_scratch_discarded_on_sleep`:
  - captures a CUDA graph on the scratch;
  - sleeps, and checks the scratch is discarded without a CPU copy;
  - wakes with `kv_cache` only, and checks the graph still replays;
  - holds a view of the pre-resize buffer across sleep/wake; once it is released, the next resize unmaps it, and a later wake does not remap it.
- New unit test `test_reentered_tag[x-freed|x-alive]`: enters a tag and allocates X, enters it again and allocates Y, frees X before or after the second entry, enters a third time and checks that only Y is still mapped; then writes Y, sleeps, wakes, reads Y back and calls `release_pools()`. With only `cumem.py` reverted to main, `[x-alive]` fails 5 of 5 runs (`assert 134217728 == 67108864`: X is never freed through `my_free`), and without that assert `wake_up()` raises `CUDA Error: invalid argument` on X's stale handle.
- Regression tests:
  - `tests/basic_correctness/memory/cumem/test_cumem.py`: `test_basic_cumem`, `test_discard_tags`, `test_cumem_with_cudagraph`, `test_sleep_with_only_weights_asleep` (all 4), `test_level2_discards_ordinary_tensor_with_weights_tag`.
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_workspace.py`.
- End-to-end on 4× GB300 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MTP and CUDA graphs:
  - Patched vs unpatched in each configuration, same image and node.
  - Memory after `/sleep`; three rounds: level 1, level 1, level 2.
  - Prompt logprobs compared before sleep and after each wake.

## Test Result

Memory per GPU after `/sleep`. Unpatched vs patched, same image and node.

| Setup | Unpatched | Patched | Saved | WorkspaceManager (unpatched) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP4 + EP4, auto MoE (FlashInfer TRTLLM) | 15178 MiB | 13856 MiB | 1322 MiB | 1322 MiB |
| TP4 + EP4, DeepGEMM MoE | 14570 MiB | 13248 MiB | 1322 MiB | 1322 MiB |
| TP4 + EP4, Marlin MoE | 14731 MiB | 13195 MiB | 1536 MiB | 1536 MiB |
| DP4 + EP4, DeepGEMM MoE, fp8 KV, mbt 8192 | 14528 MiB | 12128 MiB | **2400 MiB** | 2400 MiB |
| DP8 + EP8 over 2 nodes, DeepGEMM MoE, fp8 KV, mbt 8192 (the #59055 setup) | 16790 MiB | 12134 MiB | **4656 MiB** | 4656 MiB |

- **Memory breakdown:** in every setup the saving equals the workspace size. A memory breakdown taken while asleep accounts for all but 4–10 MiB per GPU, and no workspace memory remains.
- **Correctness:** prompt logprobs after the level-1 wakes.
  - TP4 auto and TP4 DeepGEMM: bit-identical to before sleep.
  - TP4 Marlin and DP4: differences stay within the run-to-run variation these configurations already show while awake, patched and unpatched alike.
  - After a level-2 sleep, output is garbage in both patched and unpatched runs, as expected: weights are discarded and not reloaded.
- **Timing:** sleep 8–12 s, wake 0.6–1.0 s, the same as unpatched.
- **KV cache:** unchanged. TP4 auto 202.44 GiB / 13,044,408 tokens, the same as unpatched. (Revision 0a8463b137 kept outgrown scratch buffers mapped in their pools and gave 202.24 GiB / 13,031,717 tokens.)
- **Tests:** all unit tests above pass; pre-commit passes.
- **Re-run after the pool-lifetime change (0a8463b137), same image and nodes:** asleep TP4 auto 13857 MiB, DP4 12129 MiB, DP8 12135 MiB per GPU; with #59158, TP4 9165–9293 MiB. - **Re-run after releasing outgrown buffers (21c7a0be4c), same image, another GB300 rack:** TP4 auto asleep 13859 MiB per GPU, the same as 0a8463b137 on these nodes (13859; 13857 on the earlier rack), with KV 202.44 GiB / 13,044,408 tokens instead of 202.24 GiB / 13,031,717. Every request of the gated harness bit-identical in all 10 compared rounds, including two full and two selective wakes; 4 more sleep/wake cycles exact. At sleep, the three `workspace` entries hold no free mapped memory. Unit tests: `test_cumem.py` 14, `test_sleep_mode_backend.py` 9, `test_workspace.py` 11 passed.

**Large model accuracy (GLM-5.3, TP8 over 2 GB300 nodes, `mp` backend, MTP on).** GSM8K, 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0. Each cell is accuracy, and every run had 0 invalid answers.

- The level-1 backup is 0.38 GiB smaller per GPU, because the workspace is discarded instead of copied.
- No errors on either node.

It is a separate, existing layerwise-reload gap, so level-2 accuracy is not compared here.

**Other model families (with #59158, TP4, 4× GB300).** In every phase, every request matches the first awake run exactly, text and all logprobs. The phases are level-1 full wake, level-1 selective wake, and level 2 + `reload_weights`. Level 2 + reload being exact confirms the workspace and runtime state come back.

[Bugfix][CPU] Fix macOS build on Apple Clang < 17: structured binding…
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58928.

Building the CPU backend from source on Apple Silicon fails with Apple Clang 16.0.0, even though the docs list `Apple Clang >= 15.0.0` as supported:

```
csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/fla.cpp:2312:9: error: capturing a structured binding is not yet supported in OpenMP
  2312 |         query_,
       |         ^
csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/fla.cpp:2300:9: note: 'query_' declared here
  2300 |   auto [query_, key_] = use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel ? l2norm_fwd(query, key, eps) : ...
```

(6 errors total, one each for `query_`, `key_`, `w`, `u`, `decay_mask`, `chunk_offsets`.)

**Why it happens**

In `chunk_gated_delta_rule_cpu`, the `launch_inter` generic lambda captures six structured bindings via `[&]`. The CPU build always compiles with `-fopenmp`, and Clang's OpenMP mode rejected lambda captures of structured bindings until LLVM 19. This happens even when the lambda is not inside any `#pragma omp` region. Apple Clang 16 is based on an older LLVM, so it hits this.

**The fix**

Switch `launch_inter` from `[&]` to explicit init-captures (`local_query = query_`, etc.). Init-captures create new variables inside the lambda rather than capturing the structured bindings, which older Clang accepts under `-fopenmp`. The copies are `at::Tensor` handles (refcount bump, no data copy), and every parameter of `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_inter` is `const at::Tensor&`, so behavior is unchanged. I added a comment explaining the workaround so it isn't reverted in a future sglang kernel sync.

This touches only `csrc/cpu/sgl-kernels/fla.cpp`, in one function.

**Duplicate check:** I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `structured binding OpenMP`, `fla.cpp macOS`, and `Apple clang build`.
## Test Plan

Environment: Apple M2, macOS 26.5 (arm64), Apple Clang 16.0.0 (clang-1600.0.26.6), PyTorch 2.13.0, Python 3.12.13, CMake 4.3.2. Base commit `b28c3e156`.

1. Build from source on unmodified `main`: `uv pip install -e . --no-build-isolation`
2. Build again with this patch.
3. Run the GDN CPU kernel tests, which exercise the changed function:
   `python -m pytest tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py -v`

## Test Result

- **Build before:** fails. `fla.cpp` produces 6 errors and `cmake --build` exits with status 1.
- **Build after:** succeeds.
- **Tests after:** `90 passed, 41 skipped`
  - All `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule_cpu` and `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule_cpu_two_call_split` cases pass, covering fp32/bf16/fp16 inputs and all three `initial_state` dtypes (`state_dtype0/1/2`). This exercises each `launch_inter(float{} / at::BFloat16{} / at::Half{})` branch.
  - The skipped tests require AMX or AVX-512BF16 (x86-only) and are unrelated to this change.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to help investigate the root cause and draft this description. I reproduced the failure, wrote and reviewed the change, and ran the build and tests myself.

commits.pr_title: [Metrics][P/D] Add KV-fetch stage gauges for async KV loads
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Requests waiting on an async KV load (a P/D decode request pulling KV from the prefiller, or a `MultiConnector` child loading from a KV store) only show up as `num_requests_waiting_by_reason{reason="deferred"}`, together with LoRA, grammar and streaming waits. When decode TTFT goes up, there is no way to tell whether the transfer hasn't started yet, is in flight, or already finished and the request is just waiting for a run slot.

This adds `vllm:num_requests_kv_fetch_by_stage{stage}`, a per-engine gauge that is registered only when a KV connector is configured:

- `waiting_to_start`: the request needs an async load (remote prefill requested, or an async match confirmed) that hasn't started
- `in_progress`: the load started and hasn't been reported finished
- `completed_waiting`: the load finished (or failed under `recompute`), but the request isn't running yet

The stages are tracked in the scheduler, so this works for any async connector. The counts also show up in the periodic stats log. Related to #58004, which covers the producer side.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/metrics/test_stats.py
```

E2E: 1P1D with `NixlConnector` and `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`. The decoder runs with `--max-num-seqs 2`, gets two long requests first and then a burst, so the burst arrives while it is saturated. Same again with `--data-parallel-size 2` on the decoder.

## Test Result

All pass on one GPU, except the two pipeline-parallel tests in `test_scheduler.py` that need 2-3 GPUs (same on main).

E2E: all requests succeeded, and every stage went back to 0 after the run. Peak values on the decoder:

| Decoder | waiting_to_start | in_progress | completed_waiting |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP=1 | 48 | 2 | 46 |
| DP=2, engine 0 / 1 | 32 / 32 | 2 / 32 | 30 / 30 |

The prefiller stayed at 0, since its requests have no async load. The aggregated log line looks like `2 Engines Aggregated: ... KV fetch: 64 waiting to start, 0 in progress, 0 completed waiting`.

[Bugfix][Frontend] Accept Anthropic tool_addition and tool_removal content blocks
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57324.

With tool search on, Claude Code sends `tool_addition`/`tool_removal` blocks in `role: "system"` messages. `/v1/messages` rejected them with a 400, so the client silently retried without them. Accepting and ignoring the blocks is not enough either: tools added this way are declared with `defer_loading: true`, so deferral-aware chat templates (e.g. GLM-5.1) keep hiding them.

This PR resolves the blocks into the tool list the chat template sees, following the [upstream semantics](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages): an added tool is no longer deferred, a removed tool is dropped (until added again), a `tool_definition` is declared, and a reference to an undeclared tool is a 400. The blocks are only accepted in `role: "system"` messages. MCP references are rejected, since there is no MCP connector.

## Test Plan

Live A/B on 1x H200, `main` vs this PR, same args (GLM-4.7-Flash served with GLM-5.1's chat template, which hides `defer_loading` tools; same tool format):

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --max-model-len 32768 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --chat-template glm-5.1-chat_template.jinja
```

Example request (tool added mid-conversation):

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/messages -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "zai-org/GLM-4.7-Flash", "max_tokens": 512, "temperature": 0,
  "thinking": {"type": "disabled"},
  "tools": [
    {"name": "Bash", "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"command": {"type": "string"}}}},
    {"name": "get_weather", "defer_loading": true,
     "input_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}}}
  ],
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Paris right now? Use a tool if one is available."},
    {"role": "system", "content": [
      {"type": "text", "text": "The following tools just became available."},
      {"type": "tool_addition", "tool": {"type": "tool_reference", "name": "get_weather"}}
    ]}
  ]}'
```

Plus a real Claude Code 2.1.287 session (`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true`, a local MCP weather server) through a logging proxy.

## Test Result

| Request | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| deferred tool added by reference (stream and non-stream) | 400 `literal_error ... 'tool_addition'` | 200, `tool_use get_weather {"city": "Paris"}` |
| tool removed via `tool_removal` | 400 | 200, `end_turn`: "I don't have access to a weather tool" |
| tool added by value (`tool_definition`) | 400 | 200, `tool_use db_query` |
| `count_tokens`, addition / removal | 400 | 241 / 184 (186 / 239 without the block) |
| undeclared reference, MCP reference, block in a `user` message | 400 | 400 with a specific message |
| no tool changes (incl. deferred tool never added) | 200 | identical |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CLI] Include inherited field docstrings in get_attr_docs
commits.pr_body:
Fixes #49817.

`get_attr_docs(cls)` only AST-parses `inspect.getsource(cls)` — the class's own body — so attribute docstrings inherited from a base dataclass are dropped. But `dataclasses.fields()` exposes inherited fields, so those args still get registered; the net effect is CLI args like `--chat-template` / `--lora-modules` (inherited by `FrontendArgs` from `BaseFrontendArgs`) show up in `vllm serve --help=Frontend` with no docs.

Fix: walk `cls.__mro__` base→derived and merge per-class attr docs, so inherited docstrings are picked up and a docstring redefined on a subclass still wins. Classes without retrievable source (e.g. `object`) are skipped.

## Test
Added `tests/config/test_config_utils.py::test_get_attr_docs_includes_inherited_fields` (base + derived + override) and `::test_get_attr_docs_handles_object_in_mro`.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][HiSparse] Avoid repeated prefix scans and residency updates
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

HiSparse's scheduler overhead grew with both context length and the number of resident groups:

- `plan_prefix_materialization` rescanned every computed page on each call, including the durable prefix it always skips.
- `plan_prefix_materialization` and `update_residency` ran from `HiSparseResidentManager.cache_blocks`, which the generic per-group loop calls once per resident group. With 20 resident groups this repeated the same coordinator-wide work 20 times per request per step.

At 2,048 concurrent agentic requests this used most of a scheduler core and delayed workers before their DP collective.

## Changes

- **Scan cursor:** the write-back scan starts at `max(ready_prefix_pages, importing_pages)`. Every page below `ready_prefix_pages` is already durable, so nothing it skipped is lost.
- **Once per step:** the per-step residency work (`plan_prefix_materialization` + `update_residency`) moves to `HiSparseConnectorScheduler.build_connector_meta` through `HiSparseCoordinator.advance_scheduled`, which runs once per scheduled request. The `cache_blocks` override in `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` is removed, so this PR only shrinks core.
- **Adoption publishes a block-table update:** adopting GPU copies on a host-prefix hit (#59282) now happens after the step's block IDs are captured, so `_adopt_copies` adds the request to `block_table_updates`. Without this the worker keeps reading the page from host while the coordinator pins its copy.
- **Reprefillable tokens stay out of write-backs:** like `KVCacheCoordinator.cache_blocks`, `advance_scheduled` excludes the last `num_reprefillable_tokens` (re-prefilled by multi-module MTP), so a page is not written back and marked durable before its rows are final. The auxiliary managers no longer force `enable_caching`, whose only purpose was the removed hook.

Behavior differences, both on the pressure path only:

- A request that just received its hot buffer releases its durable pages, and the low-pool watermark check runs, one step later than before. Pages written back at completion are still released in `update_connector_output`, before scheduling.
- Adoption runs after the whole scheduling pass, so a later request's allocation in the same pass can evict a copy first. The eviction watcher keeps this safe; the page is read from host instead.

## Performance

B300, one EP8 prefill node and one EP8 decode node, 2,048-concurrent Scale-SWE agentic rollouts, GLM-5.3 NVFP4, HiSparse 300 GiB/decode GPU (measured by @S1ro1 on a `7f47d2b`-based build; instrumented live-system measurements, not a fixed-batch benchmark). "Full fix" here deduplicated per-group work with a first-manager check; this revision gets the same deduplication by running it once from the connector.

commits.pr_title: [Attention][MiniMax-M3] NVFP4 KV cache on the MSA sparse attention path
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Serve the sparse MSA attention path with `--kv-cache-dtype nvfp4` on SM100, using the existing `fmha_sm100` kernels.

Builds on vllm-project/MSA#19 (merged), which makes per-head K/V slots the NVFP4 cache layout `fmha_sm100` reads.

- **MSA pin:** `vllm-project/MSA` `f355c37` → `be4a52a` (`dev`, the merge of vllm-project/MSA#19). Its CUTLASS decode and CuTe CSR (KV-outer) prefill read the NVFP4 pages in place, and `fmha_sm100` accepts them only as per-head K/V slots.
  - Moving to `dev` also brings in the public MSA #14–#18: Q8KV4/Q8KV8 indexers, a Q8KV4 NVFP4 decode kernel, and a Rubin prefill optimization.
  - `nvfp4_kv.py`, `q8kv4_decode_adapter.py` and `decode_q8kv4/` are added to the install rules. `kvouter/` is installed only because `fmha_sm100/sparse.py` imports it at module load. Of these, only `nvfp4_kv.py` is used.
- **Page layout:** a new NVFP4 subclass of the MSA sparse backend publishes `2·Hkv` head slots × 72 B per token and pins the HND (`LBHNC`) layout.
  - Slot `2·head + side` (K = 0, V = 1) holds that head's packed E2M1 data `[128, 64]`, then its E4M3 block scales `[128, 8]`.
  - So every head is one contiguous 18 KiB run of the page, `[KD0 KS0 VD0 VS0][KD1 KS1 VD1 VS1]…`, and a page split across TP ranks is a contiguous byte slice per rank.
  - With one KV head per rank this is byte-identical to the `reshape_and_cache_flash` NVFP4 layout.
  - MSA owns the layout contract: `fmha_sm100` rejects any other NVFP4 layout, and its `nvfp4_head_slot_views` derives the data and scale views. The fused insert writes this layout.
- **Prefill:** `sparse_atten_nvfp4_kv_func(kv_layout="vllm")` on the views from `nvfp4_head_slot_views`. The existing `build_k2q_csr` schedule is reused.
- **Decode:** always CUTLASS for NVFP4, at every batch size, because the Triton kernels can't read NVFP4.
  - It passes the K and V slots, `kv_cache[:, 0::2]` and `kv_cache[:, 1::2]`, along with the layer's device `_k_scale` / `_v_scale`.
  - An unsupported geometry, or running off SM100, raises instead of falling back.
  - Plans pin `decode_backend="kv_mode3"`. MSA's Q8KV4 route keeps plan-time lengths and its own page offsets, which vLLM's cached decode plans don't refresh. Using it is a follow-up.
- **KV insert (fused):** the fused qk-norm/RoPE/KV-insert kernel now quantizes K/V into the NVFP4 pages itself, in the same launch as norm/RoPE and the index-cache insert.
  - The block encoding is that of `reshape_and_cache_flash`: packed E2M1, linear K and 4×4-swizzled V E4M3 block scales.
  - Per 16-value block of `x / global_scale`: `scale = min(448, max(E4M3(max(amax, 1e-12) / 6), 1/512))` and `code = sign | RNE-E2M1(min(|x / scale|, 6))`, with zero stored as +0.
  - The quotient is a correctly rounded division (a Markstein correction of `x * rcp(scale)`), not a reciprocal multiply, so exact E2M1 midpoints round to even. The dividend is clamped to ±4096, keeping NaN, so an infinite input still saturates.
  - At a unit global scale, a cheaper path gives the same bytes for bf16/fp16 inputs. It uses the uncorrected `amax * RN(1/6)` for the scale and a truncated `x * RN(1/scale)` for the codes, with no clamp.
  - One 16-element scale group is four lanes, so the amax takes 2 shuffles.
  - SM100-family builds use `cvt.rn.satfinite.e2m1x2` and packed FP32 math: CMake gives this one file family-specific SM10x/11x targets (`10.0f;10.7f;11.0f`, or `10.xa` below CUDA 13). Other targets use a bit-exact software encoder.
  - The global scale is loaded before the PDL wait.
  - The op gains optional `kv_k_scale` / `kv_v_scale` arguments.
- **Query quantization:** when the layer quantizes q to fp8 (always for NVFP4, and for an fp8 KV cache with CUTLASS decode), the fused insert writes q only in fp8. CUTLASS decode reads it directly. Prefill and the Triton decode fallback dequantize it into the bf16 query buffer. So every token attends with the same fp8 q, and the bf16 q store is skipped.
  - The op writes q only in fp8 when it is given `q_fp8_out` without `q_out`.
- **Index q:** the fp8 index query is rounded to the model dtype before the e4m3 cast (`e4m3(bf16(q))`), using one packed cvt per element pair.
- **Not supported:** `nvfp4_4over6` on this sparse path; it is rejected at backend selection. The indexer cache stays on `indexer_kv_dtype`.

The generic `reshape_and_cache_flash` NVFP4 writer is unchanged. With more than one KV head per rank its pages use the other layout (all heads' data, then all heads' scales, per side). It also uses reciprocal-multiply math, so its bytes can differ from the fused insert's at rounding midpoints, for blocks under the 1/512 scale floor, and in the sign of zero.

## Duplicate check

No open PR adds an NVFP4 KV cache to the MSA sparse path. Searched open PRs for "nvfp4 MSA", "MSA nvfp4 KV", "nvfp4 kv cache sparse attention", "fmha_sm100" and "qknorm_rope_kv_insert":

- #56483 adds a FlashInfer MSA decode backend for the FP8 cache.
- #48994 adds a FlashInfer MSA backend for SM120/SM121.
- #55838 changes how CUTLASS MSA decode is selected for spec-decode shapes.

None of them touch the NVFP4 cache, the MSA pin or the fused insert.

## Test plan

Run in a from-source build (`TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.3`) on GB300, with `fmha_sm100` at the `be4a52a` pin:

```
pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_minimax_m3_qknorm_rope_kv_insert.py            # 80 passed
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py    # 42 passed
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3.py                              # 108 passed, 45 skipped (ROCm)
pre-commit run --files <changed>; pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual  # pass
```

- **Fused NVFP4 insert:** `test_sparse_full_nvfp4` compares the whole cache byte-for-byte against a torch implementation of the quantizer above, laid out in head slots. The inputs are the kernel's own post-RoPE K and a raw V built to hit the corner cases: exact E2M1 midpoints under non-power-of-2 scales, blocks under the 1/512 floor, all -0 blocks, and saturation (|x| > 4096 up to bf16 max, and inf). It covers 1/7/64/513 tokens, 1 and 4 KV heads, block sizes 16 and 128, padded slots, and both non-unit and unit global scales (the unit-scale path), and also checks the index-cache insert.
- **Page layout:** `test_nvfp4_kv_cache_views_address_head_slots` checks that each head's K data, K scales, V data and V scales are one contiguous run of the page, in that order.
- **Fp8-only q:** `test_sparse_full` also runs the op with `q_fp8_out` and no `q_out`. It checks that the fp8 q bytes, caches and index outputs match the run with `q_out`, and that the q slice of `qkv` is left as is.
- **Index q:** `test_sparse_full_fp8_index` requires the fp8 index q to equal `e4m3(bf16 index_q)` exactly.
- **MSA readers:** caches are written by `reshape_and_cache_flash` and repacked into head slots. Decode (including CUDA-graph replay and a batch below the old CUTLASS floor) and chunked prefill are compared against Triton on the dequantized cache, with 1 and 4 KV heads and non-unit global scales. The tolerance is meaningful: the correct path's max error is 0.02, while a wrong global scale gives 1.17 and un-swizzled V scales give 0.33.
- **Dequantized q:** the NVFP4 prefill test and a new Triton-decode-fallback test (fp8 KV, CUTLASS on but not planned) pass the fp8 q with `q_scale = 0.5` and a NaN-filled bf16 query buffer. They match Triton on the dequantized q.
- **Dispatch:** NVFP4 always plans CUTLASS decode regardless of the decode-backend setting and batch size, selects the NVFP4 MSA backend, and raises off SM100 or for `nvfp4_4over6`.

commits.pr_title: [KVConnector][NIXL] Count completion notifications that arrive after KV expiry
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

When a transfer completion notification arrives for a request the worker no longer tracks, NIXL logs an error and moves on. With the pull connector, this is the prefiller hearing from a decoder that finished reading a request whose KV lease had already expired (`Potentially invalid KV blocks for unrecognized request ...`), so the decoder may have read blocks that were already reused. The push connector has the same path (`Unrecognized request ... notif (may have expired)`). Today both are only log lines.

This adds `vllm:nixl_num_notifications_after_expiry`, a per-engine counter incremented once per such notification, in both the pull and push workers. It is kept separate from `nixl_num_failed_transfers` (transfers that fail outright) and `nixl_num_kv_expired_reqs`, and it is documented in the NIXL usage guide next to them.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py
```

E2E: 1P1D with `NixlConnector` and `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, with `kv_lease_duration=2` on the prefiller. Three normal requests, then three decoder reads that only start after the lease has expired.

## Overview

Removes the `(MI250) Basic Models Other` and `(MI250) Multimodal Processor Shard %N` AMD mirrors. Both set `no_gpu: true`, so they resolve to `CpuPlatform` and provide no ROCm coverage while occupying an MI250 agent.

- The NVIDIA/CPU parents are untouched: neither mirror overrode `commands:`.

## Validation

- `check_test_tethering.py --all` exits 0 with no output; no test file is left uncollected.
- Both YAML files parse, and the parents keep `commands`, `source_file_dependencies` and `parallelism` byte for byte against `main`.

- Guard sweep over all six `Basic Models Other` paths and the whole `models/multimodal/processing` tree for `is_rocm()`, `version.hip`, `VLLM_ROCM`, `is_cuda_alike()`, `torch.cuda.is_available`, `ROCM_`, `gfx9`, `hipblas` and `AITER`: zero hits outside `test_tensor_schema.py`, which stays on a card.

The `(MI250)` and `(MI355 DPX)` processor-shard jobs were complementary, not duplicated: the `no_gpu` one ran the directory *except* `test_tensor_schema.py` and `(MI355 DPX)` runs *only* that file. Since the excluded file is where the ROCm behaviour lives, the `no_gpu` half contributed nothing.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Responses] Use standard reasoning content-part events
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

vLLM emits custom `response.reasoning_part.added/done` events. These events fail validation against the official OpenAI Python SDK's event schema, and clients listening for standard content-part events miss the reasoning start/end notifications. This PR uses `response.content_part.added/done` with `part.type="reasoning_text"`, supported since [SDK v1.108.1, released September 19, 2025](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/releases/tag/v1.108.1). [On September 15, 2026, an OpenAI Python SDK maintainer confirmed](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/issues/2634#issuecomment-5683978987) that providers should migrate to these standard events; upgrading the SDK alone does not rename them.

**Compatibility / maintainer decision:** The current patch changes event names and breaks handlers listening for `reasoning_part.*`. Possible transition approaches, **not implemented or tested in this patch**:

- **Server-level setting (smallest change):** Keep legacy names as the default during a transition; deployments explicitly enable standard names. Existing clients need no change, but one server cannot provide different naming conventions to different clients.
- **Per-request option:** Unchanged requests keep legacy names; clients explicitly request standard names. This supports mixed clients on one endpoint, at the cost of a vLLM-specific option covering both creation and stored-response streaming.

Both can reuse the [shared SSE converter](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/3a6963664537ed21172e2ec12e96e3a2dcd3718c/vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/api_router.py#L34-L46) to translate only reasoning wrapper names, keeping the SSE event name and JSON `type` consistent without duplicating Simple/Harmony emitters. We are happy to update this PR based on maintainers' preferred transition policy.

## Claims

- Use standard reasoning content-part events in both Simple and Harmony streaming.
- Preserve the complete reasoning lifecycle added by [#35184](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35184), including the closing part event.
- Remove the two temporary event classes and update existing lifecycle checks.

## Validation

CPU reproduction against base `aee8fe202a2f` and this patch:

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Actual added/done events, Simple + Harmony (4 events) | SDK event schema rejects all 4 | Accepts all 4 |
| Streaming-event component suite | 2 new failures; 7 existing passes | 9 passed |
| Simple and Harmony lifecycle: part start/end, text, item IDs, indices, event order | — | Both path regressions pass |
| GPT-OSS/Harmony CPU serving-path smoke test: analysis → answer, analysis → function, analysis → built-in tool → analysis → answer; 1/7-token chunks | SDK final response works; 16 temporary wrapper events fail schema checks | 6/6 paired streams preserve content, order, usage and final output; all event schemas pass |

The CPU smoke test uses the public `openai/gpt-oss-20b` tokenizer and fixed Harmony conversations through the native encoder/parser, real `responses_stream_generator`, production SSE converter, and SDK `responses.stream()` via a local mock transport. With SDK 2.41.0, paired streams match after normalizing generated IDs and the two renamed event types. All six patched replays and the nine component tests also pass with the minimum SDK 2.25.0. This directly checks the affected serving/serialization path; it does not load GPT-OSS weights, run model inference, start an HTTP server, or execute tools. Clients hard-coded to old event names still need to migrate.

### Minimal reproduction: actual vLLM emitters, no model or GPU

Requires a vLLM Python development environment with its dependencies installed. Verified on Linux CPU with Python 3.12, OpenAI SDK 2.41.0 and Pydantic 2.13.5.

<details>
<summary>Run the CPU script against the original code or this patch</summary>

From the repository root:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
from openai.types.responses import ResponseStreamEvent
from pydantic import TypeAdapter, ValidationError

from vllm.entrypoints.openai.responses.streaming_events import (
    SimpleStreamingState,
    StreamingState,
    emit_reasoning_delta_events,
    emit_reasoning_done_events,
    emit_simple_reasoning_delta,
    emit_simple_reasoning_done,
    emit_simple_reasoning_open,
)

simple_state = SimpleStreamingState()
simple_events = emit_simple_reasoning_open(simple_state)
simple_events += emit_simple_reasoning_delta(simple_state, "Let me think.")
simple_events += emit_simple_reasoning_done(simple_state)
harmony_state = StreamingState()
harmony_events = emit_reasoning_delta_events("Let me think.", harmony_state)
harmony_events += emit_reasoning_done_events("Let me think.", harmony_state)
validator = TypeAdapter(ResponseStreamEvent)
failures = 0
for path, events in (("Simple", simple_events), ("Harmony", harmony_events)):
    for event in events:
        if not event.type.endswith(("part.added", "part.done")):
            continue
        try:
            validator.validate_python(event.model_dump())
        except ValidationError:
            failures += 1
            result = "REJECTED"
        else:
            result = "ACCEPTED"
        print(path, event.type, result, "by SDK event schema")
raise SystemExit(bool(failures))
PY
```

Original: all four `reasoning_part.*` events print `REJECTED`; exit status is 1. Patched: all four `content_part.*` events print `ACCEPTED`; exit status is 0. This validates emitted event schemas; it does not imply every tolerant SDK client crashes on the old names.

</details>

Component regression command in that environment:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH="$PWD" .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  --noconftest tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_streaming_events.py -q
```

`--noconftest` avoids unrelated model fixtures while importing the full production module. Applicable pre-commit checks passed. Live model/HTTP integration tests were not rerun.

## Details

[#24938](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24938) introduced these temporary types while waiting for SDK support; [the source TODO](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/aee8fe202a2fbd79a7a33cae70b310edc5960aa5/vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py#L848-L889) names that condition. [#35184](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/35184) then aligned Simple with Harmony and supplied its missing part-end event. SDK support now allows both paths to use standard events while retaining that lifecycle. The change arose while investigating DeepSeek Responses verification.

Targeted live searches found no implementing duplicate. [#56285](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56285) changes other lifecycle behavior, and [#58018](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58018) addresses Harmony zero-delta items; neither migrates these names. The same event concern was discussed in [#39426](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39426), later closed for inactivity. This patch handles the SDK-supported migration only.

---

commits.pr_title: [KV Connector][NIXL] Coalesce host-buffer KV copies across cache groups
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Addresses the coalescing item on the NIXL P/D roadmap (#33702) and the TODO it
came from, in `base_worker.py`:

```python
# TODO (NickLucche) D2H<>H2D ops could benefit from coalescing io across groups
```

When NIXL cannot register device memory (TPU, XPU, or `kv_buffer_device=cpu` on
CUDA), KV moves through a CPU staging buffer. Both directions issued one copy per
KV cache group:

```python
for group_block_ids in local_block_ids:
    self.copy_blocks(src, dst, group_block_ids, group_block_ids, "h2d")
```

`copy_kv_blocks` applies the given ids to every layer, so this costs
`groups x layers` copy operations. All KV cache groups allocate from the same
`BlockPool`, so block ids are unique across groups and the lists can be
concatenated into a single call: the same rows are written to the same layers,
and the launch count drops to `layers`.

The bytes copied are unchanged. This is a launch-overhead change, not a bandwidth
one, and it only matters for models with more than one KV cache group.

Applies to both `sync_recved_kv_to_device` (h2d, decode side) and
`save_kv_to_host` (d2h, prefill side), which share the same loop. The TODO names
both directions.

**Not a duplicate.** No issue or PR tracks this item. Checked with:

```bash
gh issue view 33702 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "33702 in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search "coalescing io across groups"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search "copy_blocks groups nixl host buffer"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search "sync_recved_kv_to_device"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search "save_kv_to_host"

# and, for each open PR that touches nixl/base_worker.py, whether it edits these functions
gh api "repos/vllm-project/vllm/pulls/$PR/files?per_page=100" \
  --jq '.[] | select(.filename|test("nixl/base_worker.py")) | .patch' \
  | grep -E "^[+-].*(sync_recved_kv_to_device|save_kv_to_host|copy_blocks)"
```

`main` still carries the per-group loop and the TODO comment, so nothing has
landed for this item.

Scope note: this coalesces across groups only, as the TODO says. `save_kv_to_host`
still iterates requests, and requests are not merged.

The `gpu_sync_allowed()` marker from #43107 is left as it is. Merging calls does
not change whether the copies are synchronous, and it reduces the number of syncs
rather than adding any.

## Test Plan

```bash
# unit
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  -m cpu_test -q

# regression across the connector suite
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/ -m cpu_test -q

# lint
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_host_buffer_kv_copy.py

# benchmark, RTX 4090 (timings and device-op counts)
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_host_buffer_kv_copy.py \
  --num-layers 16 --blocks-per-request 6 --iters 200
.venv/bin/python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_host_buffer_kv_copy.py \
  --num-layers 16 --blocks-per-request 6 --iters 20 --op-counts
```

`--blocks-per-request 6` keeps the run in the regime this change acts on. At the
default (60) each sync moves ~31 MB and bandwidth dominates, leaving launch
overhead as a small fraction of the total.

The new test fails on `main` for the multi-group and empty-group cases (three and
two calls respectively, where one is expected) and passes with this change.

## Test Result

Unit and regression, rebased onto `5707355209`:

```
tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py    76 passed, 1 deselected
tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/                             366 passed, 2 skipped
```

Lint: all pre-commit hooks pass, including `ruff`, `mypy`, and the `torch.cuda`
API check.

Latency per request-sync, minimum of 200 runs, RTX 4090:

| KV cache groups | direction | before (us) | after (us) | saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (control) | h2d | 1330 | 1337 | -0.5% |
| 1 (control) | d2h | 1405 | 1400 | +0.3% |
| 2 | h2d | 2035 | 1306 | 35.8% |
| 2 | d2h | 2143 | 1311 | 38.8% |
| 3 | h2d | 2802 | 1259 | 55.1% |
| 3 | d2h | 3178 | 1342 | 57.8% |
| 6 | h2d | 4953 | 1274 | 74.3% |
| 6 | d2h | 5978 | 1381 | 76.9% |

The "before" column grows with the group count while "after" stays flat, which is
the point of the change: one call regardless of how many groups there are.

One group is the control: both paths run identical code there, so the delta must
be zero, and it measures within 0.5%.

Device-op counts per request-sync, `--num-layers 16`, from `torch.profiler`:

| KV cache groups | operation | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | `Memcpy HtoD (Pageable -> Device)` | 32 | 16 |
| 3 | `Memcpy HtoD (Pageable -> Device)` | 48 | 16 |
| 6 | `Memcpy HtoD (Pageable -> Device)` | 96 | 16 |
| 6 | `Memcpy DtoH (Device -> Pageable)` | 96 | 16 |
| 6 | `Memcpy HtoD (Pinned -> Device)` (index upload) | 6 | 1 |
| 6 | gather / index CUDA kernels | 96 | 16 |

Exactly `groups x layers -> layers`, with index uploads going from one per group
to one.

No model evaluation is included: the change copies the same bytes from the same
source rows to the same destination rows, so decoding output is unaffected.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Integrate flash-maxsim Triton kernels for late-interaction scoring
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Replaces the vanilla padded-bmm MaxSim path (introduced in #35330, re-enabled on GPU in #38620) with vendored flash-maxsim Triton kernels for ColBERT / ColPali document scoring.

Addresses feature request #38282.

## Why this isn't a duplicate

- Issue #38282 explicitly asks for this integration; no other open PR addresses it (searched `is:pr is:open flash maxsim`).
- PR #38620 re-enabled GPU MaxSim infrastructure but explicitly deferred the kernel integration ("only cleans up the API to make integration easier") — this PR is the promised follow-up.
- PR #35330 introduced the vanilla `compute_maxsim_score_batched` that this PR replaces.

## Approach

Three scoring paths with automatic fallback:

1. **Zero-copy** (default for GPU, d ≥ 16, no chunked prefill, default pooling params):
   - Project the full `hidden_states` once via `TokenEmbeddingPoolerHead.project_batch()`.
   - Each doc request's pooler output is a `[L, d]` view into `projected_batch` — no copy, no extra allocation.
   - `flash_maxsim_rerank_direct` reads each doc at `(offset, length)` directly from the projected tensor.
   - The `[B, Lq, Ld]` score matrix is never materialized; the fused kernel tiles through SRAM.

2. **Flash-packed** (fallback when zerocopy disabled or pooling params use matryoshka / `use_activation=False`):
   - `torch.cat` all docs once, call `flash_maxsim_packed` with `cu_seqlens`.
   - No per-doc padding; kernel skips padding tokens via `cu_seqlens`.

3. **Vanilla** (fallback for CPU tensors, embedding dim < 16 (Triton `tl.dot` minimum), or `VLLM_FORCE_VANILLA_MAXSIM=1`):
   - Original sub-batched padded-bmm — unchanged.

Triton autotune keys are bucketed (`{32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096}` for Lq/Ld, `next_pow2(d)` for embed dim). `LateInteractionRunner.__init__` pre-compiles 72 bucket combinations so no autotune fires on first request; failures during warmup are logged and cleanup is in `finally`.

## Files

**New** (vendored Triton kernels — `vllm/v1/pool/flash_maxsim/`):
- `flash_maxsim.py` — main forward kernel (hardware-specific autotune configs)
- `flash_maxsim_rerank.py` — zero-copy rerank kernel (reads scattered offsets)
- `flash_maxsim_varlen.py` — packed cu_seqlens kernel
- `flash_maxsim_advanced.py` — q-reuse / split-K variants
- `__init__.py`

**Modified**:
- `vllm/v1/pool/late_interaction.py` — `compute_maxsim_score_batched` dispatches to flash when available
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/pool/late_interaction_runner.py` — kernel warmup, `_score_zerocopy`, `has_pending_docs`
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` — zerocopy branch in `_pool()` with fallback on chunked prefill / matryoshka / `use_activation=False`
- `vllm/model_executor/layers/pooler/tokwise/heads.py` — `project_batch()` method (fp16 matmul, fp32 cast of small output)

**Tests / demos**:
- `tests/v1/worker/test_late_interaction_runner.py` — updated to d=32 (Triton requires K≥16)
- `tests/v1/worker/bench_flash_maxsim.py` — detailed kernel benchmark
- `tests/v1/worker/demo_flash_maxsim.py` — copy-paste kernel/memory comparison
- `tests/v1/worker/demo_oom_resilience.py` — live server OOM demo

## Environment toggles

- `VLLM_DISABLE_ZEROCOPY=1` — disable zero-copy, use flash-packed
- `VLLM_FORCE_VANILLA_MAXSIM=1` — disable flash entirely, use vanilla bmm
- `VLLM_FLASH_MAXSIM_WARMUP_D=<d>` — extend warmup to an extra embedding dim

## Results (A100 80GB, ColBERT)

### Kernel-level on variable-length docs

| Workload | Vanilla | Flash-Packed | Zero-Copy |
|----------|---------|-------------|-----------|
| B=1K,  Ld=10-100 | 42.6ms | 0.58ms | **0.05ms** (~788×) |
| B=5K,  Ld=10-100 | 220.3ms | 2.16ms | **0.08ms** (~2,830×) |
| B=10K, Ld=10-100 | 437.6ms | 4.04ms | **0.14ms** (~3,034×) |
| B=10K, Ld=50-500 | 472.9ms | 4.22ms | **0.53ms** (~892×) |
| ColPali B=1K, Ld≈1030 | 40.4ms | 0.72ms | **0.22ms** (~184×) |

Most of vanilla's time (>90%) on varlen workloads is Python-side padding / fp32 cast / allocation, not bmm. The fused kernel eliminates that bookkeeping.

### E2E `/v1/score` (real embeddings, concurrent clients, best-of-3)

| Docs/req | Conc | Flash TPS | Vanilla TPS | ΔTput | ΔP95 |
|----------|------|-----------|-------------|-------|------|
| 500 | 8  | 6.2/s | 5.2/s | **+19%** | **+19%** |
| 500 | 16 | 6.0/s | 5.2/s | **+17%** | +7% |
| 1000 | 4 | 3.0/s | 2.6/s | **+16%** | +13% |
| 2000 | 4 | 1.6/s | 1.3/s | **+23%** | **+24%** |
| 5000 | 1 | 0.5/s | 0.4/s | **+22%** | +18% |
| 5000 | 2 | 0.6/s | 0.5/s | **+15%** | +19% |

### Correctness

- Kernel vs fp32 bmm: `max_abs_err = 4e-6`
- E2E 5K real docs: `max_abs_diff < 0.001`, zero pairs > 0.001 off, **top-3 rankings identical**

Small tail-ranking noise at positions 4-5 reflects fp16 tensor-core nondeterminism on scores within 5e-4 of each other.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_late_interaction_runner.py -v` → 4 passed
- [x] `python tests/v1/worker/demo_flash_maxsim.py` → kernel speedups & memory savings displayed
- [x] `python tests/v1/worker/bench_flash_maxsim.py` → full kernel benchmark
- [x] 5K real ColBERT docs via `/v1/score` with `VLLM_FORCE_VANILLA_MAXSIM` vs flash → score parity verified
- [x] `pre-commit run` ruff clean on all changed files
- [ ] CI on `main`

## Notes for reviewers

- The zerocopy path falls back to the normal pooler when `pooling_params.dimensions` is set (matryoshka) or `use_activation=False`, because `project_batch` normalizes before truncation — matryoshka would produce non-unit vectors. Falls back on chunked prefill for the same reason (partial cache).
- `flash_maxsim_advanced.py` (q-reuse / split-K variants) is vendored but not dispatched from the default path. Kept for potential follow-ups.
- Warmup takes ~160s cold (first launch on a host, no Triton disk cache) and ~15s warm; model load is ~80s either way.

## AI assistance

Development of this PR used AI assistance (Claude). Every changed line was reviewed by the submitter; benchmarks were run end-to-end by the submitter against both paths on real A100 hardware with real ColBERT embeddings.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Fix a chunked-prefill preemption livelock
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix a HiSparse prefill livelock: a long chunked prefill can be preempted and recomputed from token 0 forever, with no progress and no error.

Two things combine:

1. **The prefill outgrows the pool it was admitted into.** Admission caps each request's resident pages at the in-flight window (`HiSparseResidentSpec.max_admission_blocks_per_request`), assuming older pages move to host. At runtime, a request keeps its resident pages pinned until free GPU blocks fall below a fixed watermark (a tenth of the pool). A chunk that needs more than that is never switched to host reads, so the request is preempted.
2. **The preempted request resumes from nothing.** Host pages were only published once the **whole** computed prefix was durable. Host writes trail a chunked prefill by about a chunk, so nothing was published until the prefill ended. The request found no prefix hit, recomputed from 0, and was preempted at the same point again.

## Changes

`vllm/v1/hisparse/coordinator.py`:
- Publish the durable prefix of a pending publication as it becomes durable (`min(computed tokens, ready pages)`), instead of all-or-nothing. A preempted prefill resumes from it. When the whole prefix is durable this publishes exactly what it did before.
- `update_residency` also switches a request to host reads (asks for a hot region, then releases its written-back pages) once its resident pages fill the window admission reserved for it. Runtime then enforces the assumption admission makes, so these preemptions no longer happen.

`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`: `max_admission_blocks_per_request` becomes public so the coordinator can read it; `HiSparseResidentManager` declares it as `int` (always set for resident specs). No behavior change.

## Test Plan

- New `test_hisparse_preempted_prefill_resumes_from_durable_prefix`: chunk 1's writes are acked after chunk 2 is allocated, then the request is preempted; the resumed request must hit chunk 1's pages.
- New `test_hisparse_prefill_reads_host_once_it_fills_admission_window[4-True, 3-False]`: a prefill that fills its admission window requests a hot region while free blocks are still above the watermark; one below it does not.
- `test_hisparse_terminal_prefix_waits_for_all_workers_and_preserves_identity` now expects the page every worker finished writing to be published (it previously pinned all-or-nothing publication).
- Engine repro on H100: shrunk DeepSeek-V3.2 (8 layers: indexer + 8 resident groups share the GPU pool), 8192-token chunks, eager.
- `tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py`; HiSparse unit tests across `tests/v1` (`-k hisparse`).
